title: Founding Principal Engineer (m/f/d)
description: About us Most labs still count cells under a microscope by hand. It's slow, repetitive, and error-prone. We're replacing that manual work with software. By combining a standard microscope with a smartphone, we run computer vision models that locate, track, and measure cells automatically in real time. We're starting with semen analysis and expanding to other routine microscopic samples. We're a small, well-funded team in Berlin, founded in 2026. Our goal is to make automated, reliable diagnostic analysis accessible on any phone connected to a microscope. The role We're looking for an engineer who wants to own the whole platform behind a medical product: services, data, infrastructure, security and identity. A first version runs today. The hard part is making it trustworthy enough for clinical use: patient data that stays safe, an audit trail that holds up for years, and a system that recovers when something breaks. You'll own all of it, working closely with the founders and our CTO. What you'll do Own the platform end to end: backend, data, infrastructure and security. Get it ready for clinical use, and keep it reliable as we grow. Build identity, access and data handling that clinics and auditors can trust. Make the architecture calls: what to build now, what to defer, what to cut. Set the engineering standard and help hire the team that follows. What you bring Platforms you've built and run. You've built backend platforms from scratch and run them in production, through outages, data incidents, migrations and growth. Database depth. You know what happens under the query: indexing, locking, transactions, replication, zero-downtime schema changes, and backups you've actually restored. Security by default. Authentication and authorisation, tenant isolation, secrets, audit logging. You think about how a system gets attacked before it ships. Identity done properly. Identity providers, sessions and tokens, roles and permissions, onboarding and offboarding. Infrastructure. Infrastructure as code, containers, Linux, networking and cloud are everyday tools for you. Beyond the backend. The backend is your home, but when the product needs it, you read and change the app yourself. Systematic troubleshooting. You reproduce first and fix root causes. You work from evidence like logs, traces, metrics and query plans, and you stay calm when production breaks. AI-native engineering. Coding agents are part of your daily work. You give them good context, split work into reviewable steps, and stand behind every line you ship. Ownership. You help shape the roadmap, push back on weak ideas, set your own priorities and raise problems early. Nobody has to chase you. Strong opinions, held with evidence and open to revision. Range. You've worked across several companies, stacks or environments. How you work counts far more than how many years you've done it. Nice to have Regulated environments with audits: medical devices, health, finance. Serving ML models in production. What we offer Ownership from day one. As a founding engineer, you're part of the company through our virtual share option plan (VSOP). You grow with us. As the company grows, your role grows with it. Real influence. You decide how we build software, and you shape the engineering team we build. A competitive salary. A product that matters: a medical device for real clinics, built together with clinicians and lab staff. Flexible hours and office days. We work from Berlin and meet in person regularly, up to several days a week. This isn't a fully remote role. English is our working language. German isn't required. title: Senior AI Software Engineer
description:
At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you.

The team

NiCE Labs (nice.com/nice-labs) is where NiCE explores what's next in AI for customer experience. This role is on AI Innovation, the Labs pillar that builds and validates new AI capabilities through prototypes, so the company can make better product decisions, faster. 

We're a deliberately small, senior team of builders inside NiCE Cognigy, the AI agent platform. We operate in fast iteration cycles: spot an emerging capability, build a working prototype, validate it against real metrics (quality, latency, cost, user impact), and then decide: kill it, iterate, publish it, or hand it off to a product team. Some of our work is public, like the open-sourced Cognigy Platform MCP server; most of it shapes the product roadmap from the inside. 

We hire for product mindset and builder mentality. Everyone on the team takes ideas from zero to working software, shows them to real users, and argues from evidence. 

So, what’s the role all about?

You'll work at the intersection of frontier AI capabilities and a real enterprise product. The field moves faster than any roadmap can track. Your job is to close that gap: turn new models, protocols, and agent patterns into working systems, prove what matters in realistic scenarios, and produce the insights and reference implementations that let product and engineering teams move with confidence. 

You'll need to be comfortable with ambiguity, at home where best practices don't exist yet, and quick to move on when the results point elsewhere. 

How will you make an impact?  

  • Build agentic systems and full-stack prototypes end-to-end, shipping a first version in days and learning from real use
  • Track the frontier (new models, agent patterns, protocols like MCP) and turn the promising ones into working prototypes rather than slideware
  • Design experiments that show whether a concept holds up, measured in quality, latency, cost, and user impact
  • Work directly with internal users, product managers, and customers to validate concepts early and iterate quickly 
  • Turn validated prototypes into reference implementations and write-ups that product teams can build on, then hand off cleanly and move to the next bet
  • Give product and platform teams concrete feedback on where AI capabilities shine and where they fall short
  • Move between initiatives as priorities shift. What you learn on one bet compounds into the next

Have you got what it takes?

  • Have 4+ years building full-stack software, including things you started from nothing. We weigh what you've shipped more than years on a CV 
  • Have shipped LLM-powered systems to production:features real users depended on, not demos or notebooks 
  • Understand AI agents below the framework level: message arrays, tool calling, context management, prompt caching. You could build an agent loop from scratch and explain why it works
  • Use AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar) as your default way of working, and it makes you measurably faster, not just busier
  • Are full-stackin practice: comfortable taking a prototype from API to demo UI on your own (our stack centers on TypeScript/Node.js and React) 
  • Do your best work when the ground is still moving. New territory energises you more than a settled plan
  • Think in user problems first, solutions second

You will have an advantage if you also have:

  • A strong eye for UX/UI: you can make a prototype feel like a product, and you notice when one lacks that eye
  • Experience with voice and real-time AI: streaming, speech-to-text/text-to-speech, voice-to-voice models
  • Open-source work on agent tooling (MCP servers, harnesses, evals)
  • Experience designing evaluations for AI systems
  • Background in conversational AI or customer-experience products

Enjoy NICE-FLEX!  

At NICE, we work according to the NICE-FLEX hybrid model, which enables maximum flexibility: 2 days working from the office and 3 days of remote work, each week. Naturally, office days focus on face-to-face meetings, where teamwork and collaborative thinking generate innovation, new ideas, and a vibrant, interactive atmosphere.

Reporting into: Manager, Engineering, AI Innovation
Role Type: Individual Contributor

About NiCE

NICE Ltd. (NASDAQ: NICE) software products are used by 25,000+ global businesses, including 85 of the Fortune 100 corporations, to deliver extraordinary customer experiences, fight financial crime and ensure public safety. Every day, NiCE software manages more than 120 million customer interactions and monitors 3+ billion financial transactions.

Known as an innovation powerhouse that excels in AI, cloud and digital, NiCE is consistently recognized as the market leader in its domains, with over 8,500 employees across 30+ countries.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description: About the role 0G is hiring its first dedicated DevOps engineer to own our cloud platform end to end: infrastructure, deployments, networking, security hygiene and cost. Today that work is spread across several developers. Our platform runs on five providers: Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, AWS, Cloudflare and Vercel. It includes: Validator, seed, RPC, and archive nodes for our mainnet and testnet Confidential-computing (TEE) workloads, GPU machines and storage nodes Kubernetes clusters and managed databases A global RPC load balancer at the edge, and our web apps All together, that is more than 200 virtual machines. You will be the person who knows what runs where, why it runs there, and what it costs. What you'll own You own the platform, from the network edge to the bill. Cloud operations: provisioning, upgrades, capacity and the full resource lifecycle on Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud and AWS. That includes rightsizing and releasing what nobody uses. Kubernetes: run, upgrade and scale our clusters. Keep them on supported versions and design node pools, autoscaling and Spot capacity. Blockchain node fleet: operate validator, sentry, seed, RPC and archive nodes, including peering topology, snapshots, sync and client upgrades. Networking and edge: VPC design, load balancers, DNS, Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and WAF, and keeping internet egress deliberate and cheap. Infrastructure as code and CI/CD: every environment defined in Terraform or Pulumi. You design and run CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent such as GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, covering builds, tests, security scans and releases from commit to production, with no manual steps. Observability and on-call: metrics, logs, alerts and dashboards, including control of metric cardinality. You also run incident response and write the postmortems. Security and access: least-privilege IAM across every provider, secrets management, and no databases or admin ports open to the internet. Cost management: billing exports, budgets and alerts, tagging, a monthly cost review and commitment planning. Developer enablement: templates, preview environments, documentation and support for the engineers who ship on the platform. Our stack Kubernetes: GKE, EKS, Helm, Ingress and Gateway API, autoscaling, RBAC, network policies Networking: TCP/IP, subnets and CIDR, routing, NAT, L4 and L7 load balancers, DNS, TLS, firewalls, VPC peering Google Cloud: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Run, IAM, Cloud Monitoring, billing export to BigQuery Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Pulumi CI/CD and containers: Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), Argo CD, Docker and BuildKit, container registries Observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring, CloudWatch, Alibaba CloudMonitor Linux: Systems administration, systemd, disks and filesystems, performance debugging Alibaba Cloud: ECS, VPC, NLB and ALB, ESSD disks, RDS, PolarDB, SAE, Cloud Firewall AWS: EC2, EKS, RDS, ALB and NLB, Route 53, S3, Organizations Cloudflare: DNS, Workers, Tunnels, WAF and rate limiting, Zero Trust Databases (operations): PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, managed Kafka Blockchain nodes: CometBFT-based chains, reth and other EVM clients, P2P networking Vercel: Projects, builds, ISR, team access Confidential computing: Intel TDX virtual machines on Google Cloud and Alibaba Cloud Must-haves We want 5+ years in DevOps, SRE or platform roles, including 3+ years running production Kubernetes and owning CI/CD pipelines. Kubernetes, in depth Upgrading control planes and node pools with no downtime, and keeping clusters on supported versions. Scheduling: requests and limits, affinity, taints and tolerations, priority, and eviction under node pressure. Autoscaling with the HPA, cluster autoscaler or Karpenter, plus Spot or preemptible node pools for non-critical work. Networking inside the cluster: CNI, Services, Ingress or Gateway API, network policies, and DNS within the cluster. Security: RBAC, Pod Security, workload identity, and secrets that never sit in plain environment variables. Stateful workloads: StatefulSets, persistent volumes and CSI drivers, and backup and restore. Packaging and delivery with Helm or Kustomize, ideally through GitOps with Argo CD or Flux. Debugging a failing pod, node or rollout from events, logs and metrics. CI/CD, in depth Pipeline design: you have built and run production CI/CD on Jenkins or an equivalent (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Tekton). Pipelines are defined as code in a Jenkinsfile or workflow YAML, with shared libraries and reusable templates. CI platform operations: running Jenkins controllers with ephemeral agents on Kubernetes, or self-hosted runners. That includes plugin and version upgrades, credential handling, and scaling build capacity. Build pipelines: multi-service and monorepo builds with caching and parallel stages, and versioned artifacts. Container images built with Docker, BuildKit or Kaniko, including multi-architecture images, image scanning, SBOMs and signing. Deployment pipelines: promotion from dev to staging to production with approvals and quality gates, plus blue-green, canary and fast rollback. GitOps with Argo CD or Flux, and database migrations as part of a release. Infrastructure pipelines: Terraform or Pulumi plan and apply from CI, with policy checks and drift detection. Pipeline security: short-lived credentials through OIDC federation or a secrets vault instead of long-lived keys, least-privilege deploy roles, and protected branches. Release engineering for our chain: building and publishing node binaries and images, and coordinating rolling upgrades across validator and RPC fleets. Delivery health: you track build time, build cost, flaky tests and DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, time to restore), and you cut wasted builds with ignore rules and caching. Networking fundamentals TCP/IP, subnetting and CIDR, routing, NAT, and the difference between L4 and L7 load balancing. DNS, TLS and certificates, firewalls and security groups. Private connectivity: VPC design, peering, private endpoints, and keeping internal traffic off public IPs. Troubleshooting with dig, curl, mtr and tcpdump, and understanding what internet egress costs. Also required Production experience on at least two of Google Cloud, AWS and Alibaba Cloud, and willingness to learn the third quickly. Terraform or Pulumi in production, plus scripting in Bash and in Python or Go. A track record of cutting a cloud bill with data, through rightsizing, cleanup or commitments. A security-first habit with production credentials, and clear written communication. Nice to have Running blockchain nodes in production, such as CometBFT validators and sentries, EVM archive or RPC nodes, and snapshot pipelines. Cloudflare Workers, Tunnels and Zero Trust at scale. Alibaba Cloud on the international site, including its billing and support model. Confidential computing (Intel TDX) and GPU workloads. CKA or CKS certification, a FinOps certification, or experience moving a team between CI systems, such as Jenkins to GitHub Actions. Go or Rust, enough to read and patch the services you operate. What we offer Purpose : The opportunity to contribute to making AI a public good Growth : A self-directed environment where you can take initiative to shape your role and career Compensation : Market-competitive compensation including, for most roles, exposure to pre-launch tokens In addition, 0G Labs is committed to the health and well being of all of our team members. To that end, we provide reimbursements towards a holistic set of experiences and courses: Core self : Transcendental Meditation Mind : Landmark Education Emotion : Art of Communication Presence : Speech Coach Body : Fitness, gym and exercise memberships/classes Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: UI/UX Engineer
description: Betriebliche Steuern sind kompliziert – Steuerberatung muss es nicht sein. Für die meisten Unternehmen bedeutet sie bis heute Papierstapel, lange E-Mail-Verläufe und Warten. Das wollen wir grundlegend ändern. Bei b'steuern verbinden wir Steuerberatung, Software und KI von Anfang an miteinander. Unser Ziel ist nicht, eine klassische Steuerkanzlei einfach digitaler zu machen. Wir definieren neu, was Steuerberatung bdeutet: mit KI-Agenten, die ganze Arbeitsabläufe eigenständig übernehmen, und Software, die Menschen genau dort einbindet, wo sie gebraucht werden. Daraus entstehen Designfragen, für die es noch kaum etablierte Antworten gibt: Wie übergibt man Arbeit an einen KI-Agenten? Wie behält man den Überblick, wenn mehrere Agenten gleichzeitig arbeiten? Wann kann man ihren Ergebnissen vertrauen? Und wie gestaltet man die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI so, dass sie sich einfach und selbstverständlich anfühlt? Als UI/UX Engineer findest du Antworten auf diese Fragen – und setzt sie selbst in funktionierende Software um. Du gestaltest die Produkte, mit denen unsere Mandant:innen und unser Steuerteam täglich arbeiten. Und weil viele dieser Produkte und Prozesse noch gar nicht existieren, entscheidest du von Anfang an mit, wie sie aussehen sollen. Deine Aufgaben Die Arbeit unseres Steuerteams neu denken. Du arbeitest direkt mit den Menschen zusammen, die unsere internen Werkzeuge täglich nutzen. Gemeinsam findet ihr heraus, wo Software und KI ihre Arbeit einfacher, schneller und besser machen können – und wie die passenden Werkzeuge dafür aussehen. Die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI gestalten. Unsere Agenten übernehmen zunehmend ganze Arbeitsabläufe. Du entwickelst die Interaktionen und Oberflächen, mit denen Menschen Aufgaben delegieren, Ergebnisse nachvollziehen, Entscheidungen treffen und bei Bedarf eingreifen können. Die Mandant:innen-Erfahrung weiterentwickeln. Du gestaltest, wie Mandant ihre Steuerangelegenheiten erleben: einfach, transparent und ohne unnötigen Aufwand. Sie sollen jederzeit wissen, was gerade passiert und was als Nächstes ansteht. Selbst gestalten und umsetzen. Du gehst von der ersten Idee über Prototypen bis zur fertigen Anwendung. Du entwickelst deine Lösungen selbst und bringst sie in den Livebetrieb. Unser Designsystem aufbauen und weiterentwickeln. Du schaffst die Grundlagen, mit denen wir auch bei schnellem Wachstum konsistente, intuitive und hochwertige Oberflächen entwickeln können. Das bringst du mit Du kannst gestalten und bauen. Du hast Erfahrung darin, digitale Produkte zu konzipieren und selbst umzusetzen. Du denkst nicht in getrennten Design- und Entwicklungsphasen, sondern willst, dass aus guten Ideen funktionierende Software wird. Du verstehst Softwareentwicklung. Du hast bereits anspruchsvolle Softwareprojekte entwickelt und verstehst die technischen Zusammenhänge dahinter: von Anwendungslogik und Datenflüssen bis zu Schnittstellen und Architekturentscheidungen. Du hast ein gutes Gespür für UX. Du erkennst, wo Nutzer den Überblick verlieren, Informationen fehlen oder Interaktionen unnötig kompliziert werden. Klare Nutzerführung und durchdachte Details sind dir wichtig. Du denkst AI-native. Du hinterfragst ständig, wie du mit KI besser und schneller arbeiten kannst, experimentierst mit neuen Ansätzen und teilst erfolgreiche Workflows mit dem Team. Du übernimmst Verantwortung. Du brauchst keine fertig priorisierte Aufgabenliste. Du findest selbst heraus, was wichtig ist, triffst Entscheidungen auch bei unklaren Anforderungen und kannst sie begründen. Du diskutierst offen und konstruktiv. Du vertrittst deine Meinung, gibst klares Feedback und lässt dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen. Du sprichst sehr gut Deutsch und fließend Englisch und lebst in Berlin oder bist bereit, hierherzuziehen. Erfahrung in einem anspruchsvollen Start-up, mit KI-Produkten und komplexen internen Werkzeugen ist ein Plus. Ein bestimmter Abschluss, ein klassischer Werdegang oder viele Jahre Berufserfahrung sind dagegen keine Voraussetzung. Entscheidend ist, was du bereits gebaut hast und wie du an Probleme herangehst. Passt die Rolle zu dir? Du fühlst dich bei uns wohl, wenn du … genauso gern exzellente Software baust, wie du über gutes Design nachdenkst, Lust hast, neue Interaktionskonzepte für die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Menschen und KI zu entwickeln, selbst herausfindest, welches Problem gerade am wichtigsten ist, statt auf eine fertige Aufgabenliste zu warten, Freude daran hast, Dinge aufzubauen, für die es noch keine etablierten Lösungen gibt, gern direkt mit Nutzern sprichst, Lösungen ausprobierst und aus Feedback lernst, offen über deine Arbeit diskutierst und dich vom besseren Argument überzeugen lässt. Die Rolle passt eher nicht, wenn du … am liebsten ausschließlich Designs in Figma erstellst und die technische Umsetzung anderen überlässt, vor allem klar definierte Tickets und fertig priorisierte Aufgaben bearbeiten möchtest, feste Prozesse, enge Zuständigkeiten und ein großes Team mit spezialisierten Rollen erwartest, dich lieber auf die visuelle Gestaltung bestehender Produkte konzentrierst, statt auch grundlegende Produkt- und Interaktionsfragen zu lösen. Warum b'steuern? Eine Branche neu gestalten: Wir bauen nicht einfach bessere Kanzleisoftware. Wir entwickeln eine neue Art der Steuerberatung, in der Software und autonome KI-Agenten einen großen Teil der Arbeit übernehmen. Software und Kanzlei unter einem Dach: Wir entwickeln unsere Produkte direkt im eigenen Kanzleibetrieb. Du kannst mit den Menschen sprechen, für die du baust, und neue Ideen unmittelbar im Arbeitsalltag testen. Wachstum: Jeden Monat kommen viele neue Mandant dazu. Was du entwickelst, erreicht schnell immer mehr Menschen. Tempo: Wir deployen mehrfach täglich. Manche Features sind zwei Stunden nach der ersten Idee schon im Einsatz. Flache Strukturen: Wir arbeiten selbstorganisiert. Es zählt das beste Argument, nicht der Titel oder die lauteste Stimme. Kompetitives Gehalt: Wir bieten eine attraktive Vergütung abhängig von Erfahrung, Fähigkeiten und Impact. Arbeitsort: Unser Büro am Hackeschen Markt mit lebendiger Teamkultur. Wir arbeiten 3–5 Tage pro Woche gemeinsam vor Ort. Deine Bewerbung Ein Anschreiben brauchst du nicht. Zeig uns lieber etwas, das du gestaltet und selbst gebaut hast und auf das du stolz bist. Erzähl uns in ein paar Sätzen, welches Problem du gelöst hast, welche Entscheidungen du dabei getroffen hast und was du selbst umgesetzt hast. Besonders interessiert uns, wie du über Nutzererlebnisse nachdenkst und aus einer Idee ein funktionierendes Produkt machst. Wir freuen uns auf dich! Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Growth Marketing Manager
description: Growth Marketing Manager Retire the ERP Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business. We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy. We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place. Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance. Finance deserves better Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, market or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled. Light gives them a way out. We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one: Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one. Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting. Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter. We take on the ERP and the legacy point solution world with something fast to implement, AI-native from the ground up, and better the more you use it. Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée, and teams across Copenhagen, London and Stockholm, with remotes world over. The Role We're looking for a Growth Marketing Manager to join our growth team and open up the channels we haven't really touched yet. We've built a lean, efficient demand generation engine on the core paid channels you'd expect at a Series A B2B company, with Google Ads and LinkedIn doing the heavy lifting. It works, and it fills our pipeline every month. Now we want to find the next sources of pipeline, and we need someone who knows how to build them from scratch. You'll work alongside our Senior Growth Marketing Manager, VP Marketing and the wider marketing team, with the freedom to test, learn and scale the channels that move the number. You'll sit close to sales, product and design, and you'll own the results of everything you launch. We may hire more than one person through this process, so if you go deep on some of these channels rather than all of them, we still want to hear from you. What You'll Be Doing Building a referral programme that turns happy customers, partners and finance leaders into a steady source of pipeline. Running G2 and Capterra campaigns that put Light in front of buyers at the moment they compare options, and turning our reviews into proof across every channel. Launching and scaling Meta Ads for B2B, testing creative and audiences until you find what drives qualified pipeline. Finding the creators and influencers finance teams follow, writing briefs that land and scaling their content into campaigns that drive pipeline. Growing our presence across search and AI answer engines, so that when a finance leader asks Google or ChatGPT about ERP alternatives, Light shows up. Setting up measurement for each new channel with RevOps, so we know what every dollar returns. Sharing what you learn with the team, doubling down on what works and cutting what doesn't. What We Think* You'll Need Enough years in growth to know how to take a channel from zero to pipeline at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company. Hands-on experience across referrals, review sites, Meta Ads, influencer marketing or SEO and GEO. We don't expect you to master all five, so show us where you go deep. A test-and-learn mindset, with the discipline to measure every experiment against pipeline and revenue. Comfort with numbers and tools, from ad platforms to HubSpot to spreadsheets. An eye for creative and a feel for what makes finance people stop scrolling. Deep curiosity about how AI is reshaping marketing, finance and the companies we serve. A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant assholes here, please. *If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don't tick every box, we'd still love for you to reach out and convince us you're the right person. The Good Stuff A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in Copenhagen. A competitive salary and potential stock options. 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays in the country where you're based. Regular socials and two company offsites a year. The chance to build new growth channels from the ground up at a company defining a new category. Light is an equal opportunity employer. The Famous Last Words We've proven the core of our growth engine works. Now we want to see how far it can go, and we want you to build the parts we haven't tried yet. If you love starting channels from scratch and watching them turn into pipeline, let's talk. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Solutions Engineer
description: Retire the ERP. Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our AI-native financial platform gives modern, global companies automated accounting, real-time reporting and financial flows that move at the speed of the business. In a short time we've become the operating core for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot. Multinational companies don't stop at one market, and neither do we. Come help us take Light into Benelux, Latin America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific, and make it the global default for next-gen finance. The role TLDR: Own pre-sales from first discovery to signed contract across four growth regions, and build the local know-how that lets Light win there at scale. Every new market brings its own GAAP, tax rules, e-invoicing mandates, banks and incumbent ERPs. Finance leaders there want proof that Light handles their reality, not just the UK or US version of it. You'll work hand in hand with Account Executives in each region, pull in Product and Engineering when a requirement is new, and as a senior early hire you'll define how we sell technically in markets where we're starting from scratch. What you'll do Run the technical sales cycle. Lead discovery, solution design and tailored demos for CFOs, controllers and finance teams at multinational companies across Benelux, LATAM, the Middle East and APAC. Own the hard questions. Handle objections on integrations, data migration, security, controls and audit trail, and run proofs of concept against each prospect's own data and success criteria. Make Light local. Map country requirements such as local GAAP and IFRS, VAT and GST, e-invoicing (Peppol, CFDI, NF-e, ZATCA), multi-currency and statutory reporting to how Light handles them, and flag clearly where it doesn't yet. Build the regional playbook. Create demo environments, localized scenarios, RFP answers and technical collateral for each market, so the next deal there moves faster. Work with local partners. Support accounting firms, implementation partners and resellers in each region with technical enablement and joint deal work. Feed the roadmap. Turn what you hear in each market into clear localization priorities for Product and Engineering, and use AI tooling to cut the time each evaluation takes. What you'll bring 3+ years as a Solutions Engineer, Solutions Consultant or Pre-Sales lead for ERP or finance software, ideally vendor side, with a record of closing complex multi-entity deals. A strong accounting foundation: close, consolidation, intercompany, multi-currency, revenue recognition and controls, with hands-on knowledge of local requirements in at least one of our growth regions. Hands-on experience with at least one major ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics or Workday) and real implementation work: data migration, integrations, APIs. Experience selling across countries and cultures, and comfort working across time zones and travelling regularly to customers. Executive presence and crisp writing. You make complex things simple, in a demo, a workshop or a one-page proposal. Genuinely AI-native. You've changed how you work because of AI tooling, not just added it to your workflow. Bonus points Professional fluency in Dutch, French, Spanish, Portuguese or Arabic, in addition to English. A qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CPA or a local equivalent), or a background at a Big 4 or regional accounting firm desirable Experience being the first technical hire in a new region and building its playbook. You've configured AI agents in production or built your own tools with them. Probably not for you if: you've used ChatGPT once and weren't impressed, or you'd rather follow a proven playbook than write the first one. title: Payments Risk Analyst
description: Hi there! Thanks for stopping by 👋 Are you actively looking for a new opportunity? Or just checking the market? Well… you might just be in the right place! We’re looking for an experienced Payments Risk Analyst II based in Belfast to join our Global Risk team. In this role you will independently manage less-defined and more complex risk work while contributing to team projects and operational improvements. This role builds on Analyst I capability by recognising patterns, expanding findings, suggesting solutions, and applying sound judgement with minimal direction.   What you’ll be doing: Reporting to the Risk Operations Lead, you will be responsible for daily monitoring within multiple risk queues along with various operational tasks including but not limited to: Manage complex transaction, merchant, onboarding, fraud, credit, and compliance cases across risk queues, owning end-to-end assessments using merchant,business, account, transaction, and other risk signals. Apply company, partner, supportability, and restricted-product policies to less-defined reviews with minimal direction, weighing competing factors and making sound decisions with imperfect information. Use reports, risk signals, case trends, operational data, and web-service tools to identify emerging threats, high-risk or suspicious activity, and opportunities for proactive mitigation. Balance portfolio protection and chargeback risk by assessing chargeback likelihood alongside the merchant’s capacity to repay. Resolve compliance violations and complex cases, identify material risks, escalate unresolved issues appropriately, and contribute to resolution and follow-up. Identify recurring issues, control gaps, and risk patterns across tools, workflows, queues, policies, and playbooks, and recommend practical improvements. Produce concise case summaries, findings, recommendations, and decision rationale; maintain accurate documentation and contribute to knowledge material, playbooks, and team learning. Lead complex customer communications and collaborate with Support, FS Merchant Services, Product, risk analysts, and other teams to resolve shared problems. Contribute to incidents, complex reviews, trend investigations, projects, process improvements, and team best practices while prioritising competing work effectively. What you need to bring: We are looking for a highly analytical and collaborative professional with experience within a relevant analyst role along with: 2 years of experience in payments, fraud, credit risk, compliance, or financial services operations or related discipline. Exposure to structured workflows, case management, queues, or service-level targets. Experience working with written procedures and maintaining accurate records. Interest in deepening existing knowledge on fraud, credit risk, merchant risk, and payments and suggesting improvements based on said knowledge. Knowledge of Card Scheme rules and regulations Understanding of the full Chargeback flow and process - Understanding chargeback risk timeframes. Strong working knowledge of Excel/Google Sheets Good conceptual thinking with proven analytic, problem-solving and effective reporting skills Experience managing structured case work with increasing complexity and limited direction. Ability to work independently and make decisions based on available information Ability to work in a dynamic fast-paced environment with tight deadlines We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try! What’s in it for you: Come live the Lightspeed Experience… Genuine career growth opportunities based on performance within a company that's continuously expanding Work with highly skilled people who are as passionate about Fraud & Risk as you are An environment that encourages initiatives and leadership Work in a team big enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact Fun activities with your teammates & social events throughout the year Opportunity to learn, expand your skill set, forge wonderful relationships and make your mark within the diverse and inclusive Lightspeed culture, a true Canadian tech success story … and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy and healthy: Lightspeed equity scheme (we are all owners) Flexible Paid Time Off - providing you the freedom to take time off however you like Private Medical Insurance and cash health plan for optical, dental and more. Health & Wellness Credit- expense up to 400 GBP per year towards your gym membership, yoga classes, a new bike or whatever else you do for your health Mental Health Support through the LifeWorks and Modern Health Apps- whether it is meditation, coaching or counselling you need - each employee gets access to this platform Time off to volunteer and give back to your community Transit / parking benefit - for when you need to travel to the Belfast office A variety of drinks & snacks in our offices in Belfast. To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Where to from here? Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here . Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. title: Staff Engineer, EU Infrastructure
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About the Team

Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you’ll be doing

You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We’re determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you’ll be pivotal in making this reality.

Day-to-day in this role you’ll:

  • Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost.
  • Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs.
  • Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads.
  • Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently.
  • Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery.
  • Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.
  • Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.
  • Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

  • Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus.
  • Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.
  • A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.
  • Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

What we offer

  • Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence.
  • Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company.
  • Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US.
  • Growth. Room to expand your scope, whether through deeper technical leadership or broader cross-domain influence.
  • Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. title: Staff Technical Programme Manager, Systems Software
description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

Role:

System Software builds the software that runs IonQ's quantum computers: the runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport software that sit between the Quantum Operating System and the hardware. It is where a next-generation system either comes together or doesn't.

We're hiring a Staff Technical Programme Manager to lead delivery across this stack. You'll report to the Group Program Manager, Software in our Programme Management Office and be matrixed to the VP, Software for day-to-day work.

You'll work across five engineering teams (runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport) and the interfaces between them and their cross-functional stakeholders, serving several next-generation system programmes at once, with hardware being co-developed alongside the software and teams in both Oxford and the US. Those programmes draw on the same engineers, so the central problem of this role is making sure that capacity is spent by decision, not by default.

We run a centralised PMO model. This role will not own engineering headcount or define product but it will make the programme around those things run. It carries real ownership of delivery: the plan, the trade-offs put in front of decision-makers, and the honesty of the status. In this role you will interface with everyone from technical software engineers to a wide range of the most senior stakeholders. You will also coordinate with your fellow programme managers, across Science, Infrastructure and broader Software teams, making sure all plans are shared and coordinated, rather than operating in silos.

Turning a research-grade quantum system into a dependable product is a problem nobody has finished solving, and the delivery standard you'll work within is being built now. If writing the first version of the plan sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

 

Responsibilities:

In this role you will own the end-to-end delivery of the Systems Software roadmap across several concurrent programmes including managing dependencies between hardware, science and systems integration teams. You will partner closely with engineering leadership, the engineering teams run the day to day planning and boards, you will provide the direction that creates incremental milestones that ship.

You will identify risks and blockers early and work with the teams to resolve them. You will also run intake and triage, so requests reach the right team with the right priority and engineers can stay focused on planned work.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Make contention visible: when two programmes need the same team in the same quarter, bring it to the right decision-maker with the options and a recommendation before it becomes a slip.

  • Keep the systems of record honest. Requirements, plans, schedules and Jira drift apart; you'll close the gap and automate the checking.

  • Make invisible work visible: on-call load, sustaining work and technical debt tracked as rigorously as feature delivery.

  • Surface risks early, before you have a full solution or complete alignment. We'd rather hear it messy and on time.

  • Run intake and triage so requests reach the right team, with priority set by the people who own it, and engineers stay on planned work.

  • Work hand in hand with the Quantum Systems Infrastructure and Science TPMs in Oxford and the Software TPMs in the US: shared processes where teams meet, and no duplicated ceremonies, boards or reports.

  • Write concise, plain-English status on progress, risks and decisions for programme directors, engineering leaders and senior leadership.

  • Help shape how IonQ runs software delivery across sites, working with the Group Program Manager, Software on the shared delivery standard.

 

Requirements:

You will have significant experience running technical programmes across several software teams, ideally in systems, embedded, compiler or platform software. You can discuss scope and trade-offs directly with engineering leads, read and reason about code, and re-plan when a timeline is no longer realistic. You will have a track record of leading teams through genuine ambiguity, writing the first version of the plan when there isn't one, not just executing a defined one.

You can break broad problems down into specific, assignable actions, and you have designed a team's operating cadence before. No quantum background is needed. Experience of software that works closely with hardware, for example in labs, robotics, aerospace or scientific instruments, would be beneficial.

You’d be a great fit with:

  • A habit of turning diffuse problems into specific, minimal, assignable asks.

  • Technical fluency to engage engineering leads directly on scope and trade-offs, and comfort reading and reasoning about code.

  • Willingness to re-baseline against reality rather than defend dates that have stopped being true, and the judgement to tell a target that motivates from one that just generates fiction.

  • Experience with software that works closely with hardware: labs, robotics, aerospace, scientific instruments or similar.

  • A chase-without-nagging, escalate-without-drama style, and a clear sense of the difference between a risk and a noise.

  • AI as a core part of how you work, for example agent-driven tracking, reconciliation or reporting.

  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication with both technical and senior stakeholders.

Additional desirable skills include capacity and staffing modelling, designing operating cadences and experience leading work across sites and time zones. Experience working with programmes and systems such as Jira, Confluence and GitHub, with a preference for lightweight processes, is also helpful.

  • Working with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and suppliers on source inspection, first article inspection and quality problems

You will bring six or more years of related experience in a regulated manufacturing environment, including proven PCBA inspection to IPC-A-610 and experience of aerospace inspection processes and standards. You will have hands-on experience of controlling nonconforming product and of the Material Review Board process, and of using a Quality Management System or ERP nonconformance module to raise, track and close records and actions.

title: Account Executive, Deployments
description: Accelerating embodied AGI. The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries. Most sales roles hand you a territory, a playbook and a quota. This one hands you a market that does not exist yet. We are looking for a builder: someone who would rather create a market than inherit one. Our first enterprise customers are live and the signal is clear. Everything after that is yours to build. Putting physical AI onto a production line is not a software sale. It reaches the plant manager, the COO, the unions, health and safety, IT, procurement, and often the CEO. Deals take time, run through site visits and technical assessments, and are won on trust. Your job is to close our first deals in the UK and turn them into a market we own.   We look for ownership, high agency and low ego, someone who wants to shape both our customer base, shape how we sell and succeed. What You Will Do Close our first enterprise deals in the UK. Own each one end to end, from first conversation to signed contract. Run the full cycle: discovery, NDAs, use cases and footage, site visits, and a technical deployment assessment covering hardware, data, investment and timeline. Seek the truth on every deal. Navigate the whole buying group: plant managers, COOs, trade unions, health and safety, procurement, and the board. Bring each of them along. Build your own pipeline from zero. There is no SDR behind you yet. Find the industrial champions in the UK and get in the room. Develop the playbook as you go: who we sell to, how we price, what wins and what does not. The next ten sellers will run on what you build. Take what you learn on the floor back to product, research and deployment. You have closed long, complex deals with many stakeholders, and you know how to keep them moving when they stall. At your best in ambiguity. No map, no precedent, no one to ask. You sell a vision and people trust you with it. Honest, likeable, low ego, high standards. Willing to get your hands dirty. You build the account lists, write the proposals, and go to site yourself. Based in London, in the office, with regular travel to customer sites. Nice to Have You have sold to operations buyers: plant or site managers, COOs, heads of manufacturing or logistics. You have run pilots, POCs, or hardware-plus-software deals. You have been early somewhere: founding AE, first sales hire, or early Head of Sales. A background in operations consulting, VC, or as a founder. Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it. Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem. Then a decision, usually within a few days. Pay Transparency Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting. What We Offer Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter. Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval. title: Security Engineer III - Detection & Response
description: An Introduction to Primer Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform. Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on. Watch our showcase > Read up on our $100m Series C Learn more about our culture > Primer processes payments for some of the world's best companies, which makes us an attractive target and means getting detection and response right really matters. We're looking for a Security Engineer to join our Detection & Response function and own a meaningful slice of how we detect, investigate and respond to threats across our cloud infrastructure and SaaS estate. You'll write and tune the detections in our SIEM, build the automation that speeds up how we react, and be a first responder when something looks wrong. You'll have real ownership of the areas you work on, and the freedom to shape how we detect and respond to threats across them. You'll also work closely with our Application Security/Product Security engineers: what we learn from detections and incidents shapes how we build, and what they know about our products shapes what we look for. What you'll be doing Detection Build, tune and maintain detections in our SIEM (Elastic), and identify opportunities to onboard new log sources (e.g. AWS, Google Workspace, Kubernetes) and build new detections on top of them. Find what our current detections miss, and keep the rule set lean by removing what no longer adds value. Use Python and Terraform to build and maintain the infrastructure behind your detections and tooling. Response Own investigation: triage, investigate, escalate and resolve security incidents, and write up findings clearly enough to stand on their own Lead routine incidents end to end, and take a clear role in larger ones, whether that's driving the investigation or keeping stakeholders informed Build runbooks and automations (Python, Tines or similar) to cut manual work out of triage and response Join our on-call rotation for incident response and monitoring Across both Make and document risk decisions in your area, and know when to pull in others. Keep the controls you own audit-ready and contribute evidence for audits (e.g. SOC 2, PCI DSS). Use AI tools to work faster across detection and response, from drafting rules and queries to summarising investigations, while maintaining a healthy level of scepticism. What we're looking for Real experience responding to security incidents, from first alert through to write-up Hands-on experience writing and tuning detections in a SIEM (Elastic, Splunk or similar), using frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK to reason about coverage Experience with cloud-native detection and response in AWS or Google Cloud Comfortable with Python or Go for scripting and automation Clear, structured written communication, including under pressure Nice to have Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code Experience with no-code security automation or SOAR-style tooling Exposure to compliance frameworks like PCI DSS, SOC 2 or ISO27001 Background in fintech, payments or another regulated industry Experience using AI tools or agents in security work, and a clear view of where they help and where they don't ✅ A typical interview process An initial intro call with a Talent Partner An interview with the Hiring Manager Challenge Stage - Contextualised to the role A final, values-alignment interview What's the culture like at Primer? We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants. We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities. The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone. description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.   About the team The Global Risk team at Airwallex plays a critical role in enabling the company’s growth by building a strong, scalable, and globally consistent approach to risk management. The team works across the business to define risk appetite, develop frameworks and policies, support strategic decision-making, and provide oversight of key risks as Airwallex expands across products, markets, and regulatory environments. You’ll be part of a highly collaborative group that partners closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Financial Crime Compliance, Regulatory Compliance, and Legal teams to help Airwallex grow responsibly and with confidence. This is a team where you’ll tackle complex, high-impact challenges, shape how risk is managed at a global fintech, and help build the foundations for long-term scale. What you'll do As Senior Director, Enterprise Risk Management, you will shape and scale Airwallex’s enterprise risk management capability across the US and EMEA, helping ensure risk management is a strategic enabler of growth rather than a check-the-box exercise. You will translate Board-approved risk appetite into practical decision-making, strengthen governance and reporting, guide major product and organization changes, and help the company stay resilient as it grows across markets, products, and regulatory environments. You will work closely with the Chief Regulatory and Compliance Officer and senior leaders across the business to turn complex risk signals into clear action, while building a strong and practical risk culture across the organization. This role is based in the US or EMEA. Responsibilities: Lead the evolution of Airwallex’s enterprise risk architecture, including risk appetite, taxonomy, governance standards, escalation protocols, and enterprise-wide oversight, ensuring the framework remains aligned with business strategy and global growth priorities. Translate complex risk data, issues, and trends into clear, decision-useful reporting for the C-suite, Board committees, and external stakeholders, and act as a trusted independent advisor who can challenge initiatives that exceed approved risk appetite or outpace control maturity. Oversee risk-informed change governance for new products, new markets, major systems changes, and structural changes, ensuring governance supports business velocity while maintaining effective control standards and clear accountability for remediation of material issues. Own and continue to strengthen the enterprise crisis management framework, including escalation triggers, governance, and executive response mechanisms, while improving preparedness for severe but plausible events across operational, regulatory, technology, and business domains. Drive a unified, risk-aware culture across the organisation by championing consistent adoption of enterprise risk standards, reinforcing first line ownership, and promoting risk management as a shared responsibility and competitive advantage. Build and lead a high-performing global second line team, partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Operations, Commercial, Compliance, Legal, Treasury, Finance, and regional leadership to support Airwallex’s next phase of scale with more data-driven and technology-enabled risk oversight. Who you are We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory. Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Law, STEM, or another relevant quantitative field. 10 to 15+ years of experience in risk management, operational risk, enterprise risk, compliance, controls, or audit within financial services, fintech, payments, banking, or another highly regulated environment. At least 5+ years leading enterprise risk management, operational risk, or governance programmes in a complex, matrixed, multi-jurisdiction organisation. Proven experience designing, building, or scaling second line of defense frameworks, including risk appetite statements, risk taxonomies, governance processes, and escalation mechanisms. Strong familiarity with the regulatory environment relevant to electronic money institutions and payments firms, including practical exposure to regulators such as the FCA, DNB, Bank of Lithuania, MAS, and FinCEN. Demonstrated experience preparing risk papers and communicating effectively with senior executives, Board or committee audiences, regulators, or auditors, with excellent written and verbal communication skills. Experience defining crisis or incident governance frameworks and leading or supporting executive-level response to material operational, regulatory, or business events. A high-ownership, pragmatic approach, with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities and significant cross-functional collaboration. title: AI Research Scientist - Datadog AI Research (DAIR)
description:
As a Research Scientist on our team, you will partner with Research Engineers, working on fundamental research problems and collaborating with Datadog's product and engineering teams to translate research advances into products.

 

Building on our track record of AI-powered solutions (e.g., Bits AI, Bits Evolve, and our time series foundation model), Datadog AI Research tackles high-risk, high-reward problems grounded in real-world challenges in cloud observability and security.

 

We are focused on two research areas:

 

  1. World Models for Observability -- Training multimodal foundation models that learn the joint dynamics of distributed systems across metrics, traces, logs, topology, and events. These models power advanced forecasting, anomaly detection, root cause analysis, counterfactual simulation ("what if?"), and provide a learned planning backbone for our autonomous agents.
  2. Trained Agents for Observability -- Post-training models to operate autonomously across Datadog's domain. SRE incident response is our first target, with a clear path to code repair, security response, and infrastructure optimization. We build the simulation environments, RL training loops, and evaluation infrastructure needed to train agents that match or surpass frontier models at a fraction of the cost.

 

What You'll Do:

 

  • Conduct research in generative AI and machine learning, building specialized foundation models and trained agents for observability
  • Train multimodal models on large-scale, diverse telemetry data (metrics, logs, traces, topology, events) using distributed training infrastructure
  • Design and build simulated environments and RL training loops for on-policy agent training and evaluation
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering) to integrate capabilities like multimodal world modeling and autonomous agents into Datadog's products
  • Stay at the forefront of foundation models, world models, and RL-based agent research
  • Contribute to research publications, present at top-tier conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML), and help open-source key model artifacts and benchmarks

 

Who You Are:

 

  • You hold a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field, with deep expertise in areas like generative modeling, world models, AI agents, reinforcement learning, or multimodal learning (or have equivalent experience)
  • You have extensive experience designing and implementing deep learning models and agents, with a strong background in distributed training frameworks (e.g., DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM) and ML libraries (PyTorch)
  • You have a track record of impactful publications at top-tier venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, TMLR)
  • You are familiar with efficient training, post-training, and inference techniques for large foundation models
  • You can explain complex models and research findings to both technical and non-technical audiences

 

Bonus Points (any of the following):

 

  • Experience bridging research and real-world product applications, especially with large foundation models, world models, or RL-trained agents
  • Passion for pushing the boundaries of AI with a focus on customer impact and scalable deployment
  • Experience writing production data pipelines and applications
  • Hands-on experience with GPU programming and optimization, including CUDA

Cognite operates at the forefront of industrial digitalization, building AI, and data solutions that solve the world’s hardest, highest-impact problems. With unmatched industrial heritage and a comprehensive suite of AI capabilities, including low-code AI agents, Cognite accelerates the digital transformation to drive operational improvements.

We thrive in challenges. We challenge assumptions. We execute with speed and ownership. If you view obstacles as signals to step forward - not backwards - you’ll feel right at home here. 

Our Moonshot is bold: Unlock $100B in customer value by 2035, and redefine how global industry works. Join us in this venture where AI and data meet ingenuity, and together, we will forge the path to a smarter, more connected industrial future.


 

About the Role

As a Deployment Strategist, you are the owner of the customer's problem and the value we promise to deliver. You are the bridge between a customer's business objective and our technical delivery team, accountable for the "why" and the "what", while Solution Architects and Data Engineers own the "how".

You will work with senior customer stakeholders to scope value, define pilots and releases, steer delivery through to go-live, and drive adoption so that value is actually realized after launch. You combine the discipline of a program manager with the product thinking of a field product owner, and you are as comfortable in a steering committee as you are in a working session with plant engineers.

This is a hands-on role. You are expected to shape the engagement, not just report on it.

What You'll Do

Scope and define value

  • Partner with Revenue to run discovery, map stakeholders, and translate business problems into a clearly scoped engagement (outcomes, MVP, success criteria, timeline, commercial boundaries).
  • Build value cases and success metrics with the customer, and keep them visible throughout delivery.
  • Define what "done" and "valuable" mean for each release, and manage scope against them.

Own delivery outcomes

  • Lead engagements end to end, from kickoff through go-live, using an iterative, continuous-delivery approach.
  • Prioritize the backlog with the customer and the delivery team, and make trade-off decisions on scope, timeline, and quality.
  • Manage risk, dependencies, and escalations across customer, partner, and internal teams, and unblock technical and political issues early.
  • Own delivery health: plan, margin, forecast, resourcing needs, and status reporting.

Drive adoption and value realization

  • Own the path from go-live to measurable usage: adoption plans, enablement and training, user feedback loops, and health indicators.
  • Identify blockers to adoption and expansion signals early, and act on them with the account team.
  • Prepare a clean handoff to the long-term run and support model.

Lead with partners and the team

  • Coordinate delivery with system integrator and partner teams, and protect clear accountability and contract boundaries.
  • Guide Solution Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists in the engagement, and coach junior colleagues.
  • Contribute to the Value Delivery playbook: lessons learned, reusable templates, and delivery standards.

Feed the product

  • Turn field insight into structured product feedback for Product and Engineering.
  • Use AI tooling in your own work (analysis, documentation, reporting, prototyping) and help the team raise its standard.

What You Bring

Must have

  • 5+ years of experience in customer-facing delivery, program management or technical advisory for enterprise software or data/AI platforms.
  • A track record of owning complex, ambiguous engagements through to measurable customer outcomes.
  • Comfort with technical subject matter (data platforms, integration, cloud, analytics, or AI/ML). You do not need to build the solution, but you must understand it well enough to scope it and challenge it.
  • Executive-level communication: you can present, negotiate, and make decisions with senior customer stakeholders and with delivery engineers on the same day.
  • Strong command of agile and iterative delivery, backlog prioritisation, and scope management.
  • Fluent English and ideally French
  • Willingness to travel to customer sites up to 50%.

Nice to have

  • Experience in industrial sectors (energy, oil and gas, chemicals, pharma, manufacturing, utilities).
  • Experience with value-based scoping (ROI/TCO) and authoring product requirements or solution specifications.
  • Experience working in multi-vendor delivery models with system integrators.
  • Exposure to industrial data, knowledge graphs, or operational technology environments.
  • Experience in a high-growth software company or a "builder" role in a startup.

  • Align global and local teams across all functions — partner closely with engineering, UX, QA and more, with full-stack influence, keeping everyone pointed at the right outcomes.   • Proven experience as a Product Manager, Business Analyst, or equivalent role in software companies, with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets
  • Previous experience in the French energy industry — you know how the market works and its key players (e.g. Enedis / GRDF), especially around device data and market flows. Experience with energy management or utility platforms in the French market is a strong plus.
  • Fluent in French and very comfortable in English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both.
  • Confident working directly with clients — you can run a working session with client stakeholders, draw out the real requirement behind the ask, and keep senior people aligned and brought in.
  • A builder's mentality — resourceful and hands-on, comfortable building a working prototype rather than waiting for the perfect specification.

Lead escalations with clarity and urgency by defining the business impact, engaging the right internal teams, setting expectations, and maintaining customer confidence through resolution. Advocate effectively for customer needs while exercising strong judgment about when engineering involvement is required, how requests should be prioritized, and when an alternative solution can deliver the desired outcome. Maintain clear success plans, stakeholder maps, account documentation, training materials, and agreed actions so that both the customer and Constructor teams remain aligned. Partner closely with Account Management to support retention and growth by demonstrating value, strengthening executive relationships, and identifying opportunities to expand the partnership. Continuously improve how we onboard, integrate, and support customers, sharing repeatable best practices that make our processes more scalable and the customer experience more effective. Strong executive presence and the confidence to lead strategic customer conversations, including QBRs and EBRs. Strong influencing and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to create momentum and drive progress without direct authority. Strong problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to learn quickly in a fast-moving, technically sophisticated environment.
